audioDataset.subtitle: Convert, multiply and label audio for a dataset.

about.title: What it does
body: ML Toolkit is a small workbench for preparing audio datasets. Pick a tool, upload a file and download the result. It is made for the datasets behind AI music detection.

Conversion moves a file between WAV, MP3, FLAC and OGG, with a bitrate choice for the lossy formats. Augmentation makes new samples from an existing one: pitch shift, speed change, bass boost, silence trimming, mixing and added noise. Dataset organization reads a file and reports its duration, tempo, key and loudness, so a folder can be labelled without opening each track.
Processing runs on the CrownCode backend. If it has been idle it needs a minute or two to wake up, and the first request waits for it.

faq.title: Questions people ask
faq.lead: Most visitors arrive with one of these.

items.q: How can you tell if a song was made with AI?
items.a: There are a few things to listen for: vocals that never take a breath, lyrics that drift off meaning, a texture that stays the same from start to finish, endings that stop for no reason. People's songs can have all of these too. AURIS takes 47 measurements from the audio, feeds them to a model trained on 5,195 labelled songs, and shows which measurement pushed the result which way.

items.q: Does it recognise songs made with Suno or Udio?
items.a: The training set includes tracks made with Suno, Udio, MusicGen, AudioLDM, ACE-Step and DiffRhythm. New versions of these tools can fool it, so read the result as a likelihood, not a ruling.

In cross-validation it is 88.4% accurate with a ROC-AUC of 0.955, so roughly one song in nine is misclassified. The closer the probability is to the threshold (0.432), the less certain the result; the report shows this on the Certainty line.

items.q: Can it show which part of a song is AI?
items.a: It shows where the song reads AI-like. The track (up to the first six minutes) is read in windows of about 30 seconds, and each window gets its own probability, drawn under the waveform. The model was trained on whole tracks that were either all AI or all human-made, so a high window means that stretch sounds like AI music, not that an AI was used only there. A mixed track, such as a human song with an AI-made intro, can show up as a change along the timeline, but treat it as a hint.

Not on the server: the file is dropped from memory once the analysis ends, and only the result is kept for a few hours in case the same file comes back. The last audio stays in your own browser so a reload can pick up where it left off. For the FST layer, a copy goes to the mippia team's Hugging Face Space.

items.q: Is it free? Do I need an account?
items.a: It's free and there's no account. Files can be up to 30 MB. The server runs one analysis at a time, so at busy moments you wait in line, and the page shows your place.

items.q: How does a YouTube link work?
items.a: The server downloads the audio of the first six minutes and analyses it the same way as a file. YouTube blocks downloads for some videos; if that happens, upload the song as a file.

method.title: Model and validation
method.lead: LightGBM: {samples} tracks ({ai} AI-generated, {human} human-made), {features} features. Metrics use {folds}-fold cross-validation. Model files are public on Hugging Face.
method.step1: 47 features are extracted from the opening 60 seconds. The rest of the track, up to six minutes, is then read in windows of about 30 seconds.
method.step2: LightGBM estimates the probability for the opening; values above {t} are assigned to the AI class. The same model scores each window of the timeline.
method.step3: Predictions from 10 additional models are compared. SHAP computes feature contributions to the primary prediction.
method.step4: wav2vec2, FST and vocal analysis results are reported separately.
method.limit1: Performance may drop on genres and generators absent from the training data.
method.limit2: Heavy processing, electronic music, microphone recordings and low audio quality can cause misclassification.
method.limit3: Cross-validation accuracy: {acc}%. This does not guarantee performance on new tracks or prove their origin.
method.limit4: Timeline windows are about 30 seconds long, shorter than the 60-second clips the model was trained on, and each training clip was either all AI or all human-made. A window shows where the music reads AI-like, not where an AI was used.

meta.title: Privacy Policy | CrownCode
meta.description: What data CrownCode collects, how it is used and how it is protected.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This page says what the CrownCode site and its tools do with your data.

dataCollection.title: What is collected
dataCollection.content: There are no accounts. On a sample of visits the site records anonymous page-speed measurements and the page they came from. The servers that host the site and the tools (Cloudflare and Hugging Face) keep ordinary access logs, which can include your IP address and browser.

dataUsage.title: What happens to what you send
dataUsage.content: Audio, a dream text or a video link goes to the tool's server only to produce your result. Analyses are held in memory for a short while so you can fetch the result, then discarded. Crown Dreams sends the dream text, and Crown Commend the video's transcript, to Google's Gemini API to write the reply; Google handles that text under its own terms. Nothing is sold or used for advertising.

dataSecurity.title: On your device
dataSecurity.content: Your language choice, your analysis history and your Crown Fortune draws are kept in your browser's local storage and never leave your device. Clear the site's data in your browser to remove them. Traffic between you and the site is encrypted over HTTPS.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.content: One cookie remembers your language. There are no tracking or advertising cookies.

creatorStudio.title: Creator Studio
creatorStudio.subtitle: Tools for remixing and mixing tracks

about.title: How the tools work
body: Remix Studio takes two tracks, detects the tempo and key of each, stretches and pitch-shifts the second one to fit the first, and joins them with a crossfade you set. The result downloads as a WAV file.
The Multi-Track Mixer takes two to six tracks. You set each track's level and its place between left and right, and the mix is bounced to one file with its peak level normalised so it does not clip.
Each file can be up to 30 MB. Processing runs on the CrownCode backend, so the first request after a quiet spell can take a minute or two.
